newsitem.title: THAILAND: Lignite tops Thai 1996 mineral production.
newsitem.headline: Lignite tops Thai 1996 mineral production.

text.p: Thailand's 1996 mineral production rose to 22.69 billion baht ($907.6 million), up 9.3 percent from 1995, with lignite accounting almost half the production, an industry ministry official said on Saturday.
Total production of lignite was 10 billion baht, or 43.7 percent of the 1996 national mineral production, the official said.
Lignite is used mostly as fuel in electricity generation and cement production.
The other two major mineral resources produced in 1996 were zinc and limestone. About 90 percent of the production was used for domestic consumption and not for export, he said.
According to the ministry's survey at the end of August 1994, Thai lignite reserves amounted 1.49 billion tonnes for developed resources and 890 million tonnes for undeveloped resources.
The reserves could last 30-40 years at present consumption rate, the official said. No further details were given. ($1 = 25 baht)
